content: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis (ME), also referred to as Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (CFS), is frequently linked to outbreaks. This association has led many researchers and patient advocacy groups to strongly believe that the illness, particularly in its initial stages, is either caused by a contagious virus or triggered by one or more viral infections. In earlier documented cases, the terminology used to describe the condition varied significantly, even in instances where healthcare professionals at the time considered it to be a form of poliomyelitis. Additionally, the clusters of symptoms observed tend to differ between outbreaks.
